incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-9876 — CUDA_ALLOC_FAIL spike on gpu-west-2a pool. threshold breached (alloc failures > 50/m). docs.runbook.link/oom-handling :eyes:
pagerduty: Alert details: PD-9876 (P1) — multiple CUDA OOMs across nodes g-west-2a-12..15. Auto-escalation in 15m if unacked.
Alex (oncall): Acked. I'm taking lead. Tagging SRE and runtime.
Maya (eng-sre): I'm pulling node metrics. kvcache eviction rate spiked ~X10 at 12:02UTC, GPU mem usage ~97-99% on g-west-2a-12,g-west-2a-14.
John (eng-runtime): Noted. Recent rollout of batching change? Checking last deploy.
Priya (infra): No infra deploys in last hour. I see a customer workload burst from tenant: payment-ml-prod.
Alex (oncall): Priority steps: 1) route traffic away from the affected pool 2) enable fallback model variant (quantized) 3) scale up fallback pool 4) collect full nvml logs.
John (eng-runtime): Kicking fallback rollout: running the route-change script now.
John (eng-runtime): ```
# reroute traffic away from gpu-west-2a pool
./routeset --from pool=gpu-west-2a --to pool=gpu-west-2b --reason "OOM surge PD-9876"
```
Maya (eng-sre): Running quick evictions policy to free KV cache on nodes: `/api/admin/cache/evict?region=west-2a&percent=30` — firing now.
Priya (infra): Spun up 4 small instances to handle burst (autoscale group: gpu-fallback-west2) — expected ready ~3m.
Leah (customer-success): CS: 3 customers opened tickets, one reports 500 on embeddings endpoints, latency increased for 7 others. I'm preparing an outbound note.
Victor (eng-ml): Recommending activating 16-bit quantized model variant for heavy customers to cut memory. We have verified parity on recent evals.
Alex (oncall): John, Priya — confirm fallback pool readiness and warm cache strategy.
John (eng-runtime): Fallback pool healthy. Applying model-pinning policy for affected tenants: ```
POST /admin/pinning
{ "tenants": ["payment-ml-prod"], "model": "q4_16b_fast", "pool": "gpu-fallback-west2" }
```
Priya (infra): New instances are in service. LB reroute completed for ~60% of traffic away from gpu-west-2a.
Maya (eng-sre): NVML logs from g-west-2a-14: ```
[12:02:43] cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY)
[12:02:43] kernel: kvcache_evict triggered for shard 7
[12:02:44] retrying allocation -> failed
```
Alex (oncall): Good. Keep OOM logs coming, we need to know whether it's fragmentation or sustained capacity.
John (eng-runtime): Implemented per-request kv eviction threshold adjustment to 0.6 for affected pool.
Maya (eng-sre): Observing alloc failure rate dropping from 55/m -> 8/m after reroute + eviction. GPU mem usage on affected nodes down to ~82% on g-west-2a-12.
Leah (customer-success): Sent interim status to impacted customers: "We detected a GPU memory surge impacting a subset of requests. We have rerouted traffic and are using a lower-memory model variant. Expect degraded latencies for ~10-15 minutes while we stabilize."
Alex (oncall): PagerDuty: please mark PD-9876 acknowledged and set to monitor.
pagerduty: PD-9876 acknowledged by Alex (oncall). Escalation paused.
Victor (eng-ml): Suggest follow-ups: schedule model evals for memory patterns, add a regression alert for kvcache eviction spikes, and consider proactive pre-warming for large-tenant traffic.
Maya (eng-sre): Root-cause candidate: sudden tenant traffic spike combined with KV cache retention increase after the batching tweak. Will correlate with deploy timeline and tenant request patterns.
Alex (oncall): Next actions: - keep traffic routed off gpu-west-2a while we drain and reprovision - collect full heap + nvml traces from g-west-2a nodes - postmortem owner: Maya - customer comm owner: Leah. If anyone needs handoff after my shift ping @oncall-next.
Priya (infra): I'll initiate a drain + reprovision for g-west-2a-14 (highest OOMs) now. ETA ~12m.
John (eng-runtime): Saving run traces and captured kvcache metrics to s3://incidents/PD-9876/trace.tar.gz and adding link to the incident ticket.
Alex (oncall): Thanks team. I'll keep monitoring; will update this thread when we hit stable for 30m or if things regress. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: PD-9876 — acknowledged by Alex (oncall). Incident state: Mitigating. Links: docs.runbook.link/oom-handling, s3://incidents/PD-9876/trace.tar.gz
Alex (oncall): 12:22UTC update: alloc failures down to 2/m, affected customers served by fallback. Leaving monitoring.
Leah (customer-success): Noted, continuing customer follow-ups.
Maya (eng-sre): Assigning postmortem to myself. Will include timeline, mitigation steps, and action items (alert tuning, pre-warm, revert batching tweak)
Alex (oncall): Closing active pager for now; keeping channel open for postmortem artifacts.
pagerduty: PD-9876 — status set to "monitoring". No further escalation scheduled.
